newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT - Xerox Q4 earnings rise 14 pct.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT - Xerox Q4 earnings rise 14 pct.

text.p: Earlier, Xerox Corp reported fourth quarter earnings per share of $1.17 on an operating basis. Wall Street analysts had expected Xerox to earn about $1.14, according to First Call.
The company also raised its quarterly dividend and agreed to sell the Coregis business of Talegen to General Electric Co for $375 million in cash and $75 million of debt assumption.
The following is the full text of Xerox's announcement.

STAMFORD, Conn., Jan 23 - Xerox Corporation (NYSE: XRX) document processingfully diluted earnings per share increased 14 percent to $1.17 in the fourth quarter of 1996, excluding a 1995 one-time tax gain, and on the same basis, income increased 12 percent to $426 million.

Revenues grew 8 percent on a pre-currency basis to $5.1 billion in the quarter, driven by 14 percent growth in equipment sales and 41 percent growth in document outsourcing. Service and rental revenues were essentially unchanged from the fourth quarter of 1995.

"Our strategies are driving improved results," said Xerox Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Paul A. Allaire. "The increase in equipment sales growth is the direct result of our investments in sales coverage and marketing support and excellent customer acceptance of our new digital products.
"In recognition of this performance and future growth prospects, the board of directors declared a 10 percent increase in the dividend on our common stock," Allaire said.
Effective with the dividend payable April 1, the quarterly dividend will increase from 29 cents to 32 cents, or an annual rate of $1.28, to shareholders of record March 7.

Digital product revenues, which represented 34 percent of total revenues, grew 26 percent in the quarter, reflecting excellent growth in production publishing and color copying and printing. Allaire noted that the DocuColor 40 and the Document Centre Systems family each contributed 3 percentage points to the digital product revenue growth of 26 percent in the fourth quarter.

The DocuColor 40, at 40 full-color pages per minute, is the industry's fastest and most affordable digital color document production system. Document Centre Systems products can print, scan, fax and copy documents for workgroups, with all operations managed over the network from each user's personal computer or on a walk-up basis.

Black-and-white light lens copier revenues, which represented 53 percent of total revenues, were flat in the quarter. Excellent copier equipment sales growth in the United States and Brazil was partially offset by a decline in Europe, reflecting difficult economic environments in several countries as well as a strong 1995 fourth quarter.

The operating profit margin improved by 0.5 percentage points, due to an increase in gross margins and a reduction in the ratio of selling, administrative and general expenses to revenues. The worldwide work force declined by 300 in the quarter to 86,700 as hiring in the company's fast-growing document outsourcing business was more than offset by reductions in other areas.

For the full year 1996, document processing fully diluted earnings per share increased 13 percent to $3.31 excluding the tax gain and, on the same basis, income increased 12 percent to $1.2 billion. Revenues increased by 6 percent on a pre-currency basis to $17.4 billion, including 10 percent growth in equipment sales.
"Building on these successes, 1997 will be another important chapter in the unfolding story of innovative new digital products from The Document Company," Allaire said.

"Our leadership in digital, networking and color products positions us well to capitalize on the expanding opportunities in the worldwide document processing market," he said. "The accelerating growth of our digital products and our focus on productivity and expense control are expected to result in continuing earnings growth in 1997."

The Xerox chairman said he was pleased with today's announcement of the agreement to sell Talegen's Coregis unit for total consideration of $450 million and encouraged by the strong interest of prospective buyers in the remaining units of Talegen Holdings, Inc. He said Xerox expects to have substantially completed sales of the remaining Talegen companies by the end of the year, consistent with its strategy to focus on document processing.
"The good cash flow from document processing and the expected sales of the Talegen units will enable an acceleration of our stock buy-back program this year," Allaire said.
In February 1996, the board of directors authorized the repurchase of up to $1 billion of Xerox common stock. By Dec. 31, the company had repurchased 6.5 million shares for $306 million.

In the fourth quarter of 1995, Xerox reported a loss of $1.1 billion, or $3.43 per fully diluted share, including the $98 million tax gain and a charge of $1.55 billion as a result of the planned disengagement from the insurance business. For the full year 1995, the company reported a loss of $472 million, or $1.75 a share. The Talegen insurance operations are accounted for as discontinued operations.
Three months ended Six Months ended

NOTE: Document processing primary earnings per share were $1.25 in the fourth quarter and $3.49 for the full year 1996. In the fourth quarter of 1995, primary earnings per share were $1.10 excluding the tax benefit and $1.39 including the tax benefit. For the full year 1995, primary earnings per share were $3.11 excluding the tax benefit and $3.40 including the tax benefit.

Total common shares used to calculate fully diluted earnings per share were 363.7 million, compared with 363.1 million the year before. Total common shares used to calculate primary earnings per share were 332.7 million, compared with 331.7 million a year ago. SOURCE Xerox Corporation
